title: Pricing & Headcount Sensitivity — Ops Flex Plan (Q3 2026)
body:
Purpose:
Quick working draft to quantify near-term (Q3–Q4 2026) impacts from alternate pricing moves combined with targeted headcount adjustments in Ops/Support/Platform. This is a finance-first sensitivity to help leadership decide: (a) whether to pursue a moderate price change, (b) whether to implement a targeted ~10–15% HC reduction in non-customer-facing ops, or (c) a combination.

High-level summary (headline bullets):
- Baseline assumptions: FY26 ARR run-rate (internal forecast) = $72.4M; FY26 gross margin = 66%; total company headcount = 150 (end Q2). Monthly net burn (post-credits, pre-financing) = $1.2M.
- Price +7.5% (no churn assumed) increases annual revenue by ~$5.4M and reduces monthly burn by ~$0.26M after COGS and OpEx flow-through; realistic net uplift likely lower due to elasticity — model below uses 5% net retention loss in conservative case.
- Price -12.5% (to drive competitiveness) projects a revenue loss of ~$9.0M if acceptance/compression occurs — combined with increased usage this could partially offset but not fully; this scenario stresses the need for >10% Ops HC reduction to keep burn neutral.
- Headcount reduction of 12% concentrated in Platform/Infra/Support (~18 people) lowers OpEx by ~$3.2M annual run-rate (salary + benefits + severance smoothing), cutting monthly burn by ~0.27M after spread.
- Combined moderate price increase (+7.5%) + 6% HC reduction yields roughly balanced improvement (~$4.0M annual improvement) and preserves customer service SLAs; recommended path if leadership wants lower disruption.

Assumptions (explicit):
- Revenue base: $72.4M ARR (internal consensus through Q2 close).
- COGS proportion: 34% of revenue (GPU costs, cloud infra, dedicated pools). Gross margin = 66% baseline.
- OpEx split (annualized): Engineering + infra: $22.0M; GTM (sales+marketing+cs): $12.5M; G&A + finance: $6.2M; R&D/Research: included in engineering. Total OpEx ~ $40.7M.
- Average fully-loaded comp per employee: $220k (engineering), $140k (GTM), $120k (G&A). Use role buckets in HC plan.
- Severance / one-time costs: assume 0.5x monthly run rate for headcount reductions where applicable (modeled as a one-time $850k hit for the 18-person reduction scenario).
- Pricing elasticity: 0.3 to 1.0 depending on customer segment; model three elasticity buckets: low-elasticity (enterprise, 0.15), medium (mid-market, 0.5), high (self-serve/SMB, 1.0). Weighted average assumed in scenarios.
- Timing: P&L impact recognized starting next full quarter after change (i.e., price change executed in late Q3 affects Q4). HC savings phased 60% in first 3 months, 100% by month 6.

Scenario detail (select rows from the working sensitivity sheet):

Baseline (current run-rate):
- ARR: $72,400,000
- Annual COGS: $24,616,000 (34%)
- Gross profit: $47,784,000
- Annual OpEx: $40,700,000
- Operating margin (baseline): $7,084,000 (~9.8%)
- Monthly net burn (baseline): $1,200,000 (internal calc after cash interest/timing)

Scenario A — Price +7.5% (optimistic: no churn):
- New ARR: $77,730,000 (+$5.43M)
- New COGS (assume proportionally increases by 2% of incremental revenue due to usage): COGS ≈ $25,000,000
- Gross profit delta: +$4.2M
- OpEx unchanged initially -> Operating margin improves by ~$4.2M -> monthly burn improvement ≈ $350k (gross), net improvement after tax/ops ~ $260k
- Conservative elasticity adj (5% customer revenue attrition within 6 months): net ARR uplift reduces to ~$2.9M; monthly burn improvement ~ $150k.

Scenario B — Price -12.5% (market-driven discounting):
- New ARR: $63,350,000 (-$9.05M) assuming no usage offset
- COGS drops proportionally but fixed infra costs limit immediate savings: COGS ≈ $21,500,000
- Gross profit loss: -$7.2M
- To maintain cash neutrality, need OpEx cuts ~ $7.2M annual -> HC cut of ~38 FTE equiv at current cost structure (not feasible without major disruption).
- Mixed scenario: Price cut + usage growth (50% of lost rev offset) -> still negative unless paired with >=15% HC reduction.

Scenario C — HC reduction 12% in Ops/Platform (targeted exec proposal):
- HC removed: 18 FTE (mix: 10 infra/engineers, 5 support, 3 ops managers)
- Annual OpEx reduction: ~$3.2M (salary+benefits) + ~$0.25M recurring comp/contract renegs -> net annual saving ~ $3.45M
- One-time severance and legal & benefits: $850k (modeled as Q3/Q4 cash impact)
- Monthly burn change (steady state): improvement ≈ $287k/mo after full phase-in.

Scenario D — Combined: Price +7.5% + HC -6% (conservative middle path):
- ARR uplift (7.5%, conservative attr 3%): +$3.7M annual
- HC cut 6% saves ~$1.7M annual (9 FTE) with $425k severance one-time
- Combined annual improvement ≈ $5.4M -> monthly burn improvement ≈ $450k -> runway extension ~ 5–6 months on current cash + after accounting for severance and execution slippage.

Simple sensitivity matrix (excerpt):
- Columns: scenario / ARR delta / OpEx delta / Runway months added
- Baseline: 0 / 0 / 0
- Price +7.5% (no attr): +5.4M / 0 / +4.5 months
- Price +7.5% (5% attr): +2.9M / 0 / +2.3 months
- Price -12.5%: -9.0M / 0 / -7.5 months
- HC -12%: 0 / -3.45M / +2.9 months
- Combined (+7.5% + HC-6%): +5.4M / -1.7M / +5.5 months

Operational notes & risks:
- Customer segmentation is critical: enterprise customers are sensitive to sticker changes but PV of revenue loss is concentrated in SMB pool. Any broad price increase must include grandfathering/contract carveouts to avoid churn.
- Timing: executing price increases in self-serve requires UI/marketing and clear comms; enterprise requires contract amendments -> longer lead time but lower churn risk.
- HC cuts in Platform carry product delivery/ops risk: 10 infra FTEs removed would slow new capacity/product work and could increase latency incidents; we should map critical projects (net-new Dedicated deployments, Private on-premies backlog) to retained headcount before finalizing.
- Legal/compliance: severance, contractual obligations -> need HR + legal check for local regs (esp. EU/APAC).

Recommended next steps (short list for leadership discussion):
1) Approve run-of-hypotheses: build segmented elasticity model (enterprise/mid-market/smb) and re-run with customer-level cohorts (linked sheet FIN-2031 cohort model). Ownership: Ethan Morales.
2) Validate deliverability of HC reductions: require 1:1 role mapping, project slippage impact, and 60/180-day phased plan. Ownership: Sofia Kim + Marcus Liu.
3) Prepare two comms packages: (A) targeted price uplift for self-serve (7.5%) with grandfathering; (B) discount program for competitive wins with strict ROI guardrails. Ownership: GTM lead, Finance to sign off on revenue math.
4) Model cash flow including severance timing and possible financing bridge if leadership prefers deeper HC moves with cash smoothing. Ownership: Finance (Priya).

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Need updated cohort elasticity inputs (linked sheet) — current numbers are rough weights.
- Confirm severance estimate range per region (US vs. EMEA vs. APAC).
- Identify non-headcount OpEx levers (vendor contract renegotiations, committed cloud reductions) that could be less disruptive.
- Pull reconciled ARR by product line (hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private) to model price moves gearbox.

Appendix (quick calculations shown inline):
- Price +7.5%: 72.4M * 0.075 = 5.43M incremental ARR
- Conservative attr adjusted incremental ARR: 5.43M * (1 - 0.45) = 2.99M (we used 45% effective loss in earlier conservative bucket; adjust per segmentation)
- HC 18 FTE savings: avg 18 * 190k fully-loaded = 3.42M (rounded to 3.2M after contract roll-offs and overheads)

Notes to reviewer: this is a working finance sheet write-up to support the March leadership offsite. Numbers are intentionally rounded. Please flag any missing hidden costs (e.g., contract termination fees for dedicated hardware partners) and add comments in the linked sheet.

-- Priya
